Personality: Siddonrik is known as a man as cold as an ice floe on the North Sea. As the son of Haldarr, he perfectly inherited the Nords' desire to conquer the ocean, but he was mean and stingy in his dealings with others. He does not seek fame or heroic praise, but rather values ​​actual benefits and absolute obedience. He showed no mercy when dealing with prisoners of war or territorial matters, believing that weakness was a taboo in rule. He is taciturn, and his sharp eyes are always looking at everything around him, as if he is calculating the loss of every longship and the ownership of every piece of loot. For him, the authority of the family is above all else, and any challenge to the rule of the Trosnir family will be dealt a ruthless blow by him. This cold and pragmatic character makes him highly prestige among his subordinates but lacks affinity. He is a typical pragmatic lord.
Background: Sidonrik was born into the famous Nord family Trosnir, and is the son of the current king Haldarr "Blonde" and Yaminya. He grew up in the turbulent period after his grandfather Volbjorn the Hungry forcibly unified the North, and witnessed firsthand his father's difficulties in maintaining the unity of the kingdom. In order to consolidate his family's rule in the city of Trondela and Skartnaisberg, he trained on a longship since his childhood and became proficient in navigation, reconnaissance and boarding warfare. As Nordvig transformed from a loose confederation of tribes to a centralized kingdom, Sidunrik became his father's staunchest enforcer. Not only did he accumulate wealth for his family through maritime trade and plunder, but he also used harsh methods to frighten those dissatisfied Yaers who longed to return to the old times. Although the bonds of the kingdom remain fragile, he firmly believes that through iron fist rule and foreign conquest, the throne of House Trosnir will be unshakable.
